headline: The lease is up
body: Renew, move, or stop having one.

options.label: Renew for five years
options.detail: Cheaper per month, but you're locked in if anything changes.

options.label: Move somewhere smaller and better
options.detail: A smaller space that actually works for you.
options.storyHeadline: Moved to a smaller, better office

options.label: No office at all
options.detail: Fully remote — cheaper, but new hires take longer to feel real.

headline: Somebody wants a standing desk
body: Then everybody wants a standing desk.

options.label: Buy them for everyone
options.detail: The whole office, standing desks, done.

options.label: Buy one for whoever asks
options.detail: Mild resentment, but it works fine.

options.label: No
options.detail: Three people buy their own and mention it, repeatedly.
options.storyHeadline: Said no to the standing desks

headline: The upstairs neighbours are a drum school
body: Tuesdays and Thursdays, two till six.

options.label: Move
options.detail: Everyone is relieved the moment the boxes are out.
options.storyHeadline: Moved offices to escape the drum school

options.label: Buy the whole team headphones
options.detail: Output recovers. It's a faintly absurd solution that works.

options.label: Complain to the landlord
options.detail: Nothing changes. You have made an enemy downstairs.
options.storyHeadline: Complained to the landlord, to no effect

headline: Someone has started sleeping in the office
body: Not metaphorically. There is a duvet.

options.label: Talk to them properly
options.detail: You discover something serious is going on at home.
options.storyHeadline: Talked to the person sleeping in the office

options.label: Ban it and say nothing else
options.detail: They leave, quietly, within four months.

options.label: Ignore it
options.detail: It becomes normal. Normal is worse than you'd think.

headline: A second office in a cheaper city
body: Talent is 40% cheaper two hundred miles away.

options.label: Open it
options.detail: Costs come down. The culture quietly splits in two.

options.label: Stay in one place
options.detail: Expensive, coherent, and slower to grow.

headline: The coffee machine
body: The cheap one has broken again. The good one is $4,200.

options.label: Buy the good one
options.detail: It gets mentioned in exit interviews for a decade.

options.label: Another cheap one
options.detail: It breaks again in fourteen months.

options.label: Everyone can go to the café
options.detail: They were going anyway, but it stings a little.
options.storyHeadline: Sent everyone to the café instead

headline: A customer wants to pay in something other than money
body: They have no cash and a warehouse full of their product.

options.label: Accept
options.detail: Revenue on paper, a storage problem in reality.

options.label: Refuse
options.detail: You lose the customer and keep your sanity.

options.label: Take half in cash, half in product
options.detail: Awkward, but it works.
options.storyHeadline: Split the payment between cash and product

headline: Your biggest customer wants a discount to renew
body: Fifteen percent, or they'll look elsewhere.

options.label: Give it
options.detail: They stay four more years, at a lower price.
options.storyHeadline: Gave the biggest customer a discount to stay

options.label: Hold firm
options.detail: A coin flip on whether they were bluffing.

options.label: Give it in exchange for a three-year commitment
options.detail: The same discount, but with certainty attached.
options.storyHeadline: Traded a discount for a three-year commitment

headline: A customer is using it wrong and blaming you
body: Very publicly, at some length.

options.label: Fix their setup personally
options.detail: Two days gone. They become an advocate.

options.label: Reply publicly with the facts
options.detail: You are right, and you look defensive anyway.

options.label: Refund them and part ways
options.detail: Small cost, and silence afterward.
options.storyHeadline: Refunded the customer and parted ways

headline: Someone wants to buy a hundred at once
body: Cash up front, at 40% off.

options.label: Take it
options.detail: The margin is gone, and now they resell it cheaper than you do.
options.storyHeadline: Sold a hundred units at a steep discount

options.label: Refuse
options.detail: Cash stays tight. Pricing stays intact.

headline: A customer asks for a feature that already exists
body: For the sixth time this month, by six different people.

options.label: Rebuild how the product explains itself
options.detail: Six weeks of work. Support load drops sharply.
options.storyHeadline: Rebuilt how the product explains itself

options.label: Write better documentation
options.detail: Two weeks, and it helps somewhat.

options.label: Answer each email personally
options.detail: Warm, and completely unsustainable.

headline: The reference call
body: A prospective customer wants to speak to an existing one. Your best customer is on holiday. Your second best is difficult.

options.label: Use the difficult one
options.detail: A real risk they mention the outage.
options.storyHeadline: Used the difficult customer as a reference

gamble.loseText: They mentioned the outage. The deal wobbled.

options.label: Wait two weeks for the good one
options.detail: The deal cools while you wait.

gamble.winText: The wait paid off — they signed.
gamble.loseText: The deal died while you waited.

headline: A customer has been quietly overcharged for two years
body: A billing error in your favour. Nobody has noticed.

options.label: Tell them and refund it
options.detail: They tell four other companies about you, all of it good.
options.storyHeadline: Told the customer and refunded the overcharge

options.label: Fix it silently going forward
options.detail: Nothing happens, unless someone runs the numbers.

options.label: Say nothing at all
options.detail: A real chance it surfaces later, and badly.

gamble.loseText: It surfaced. It was very bad.

headline: Two people want the same week off
body: Both booked flights. Neither will move.

options.label: First to ask wins
options.detail: Clear, and one person is unhappy about it.
options.storyHeadline: Let the first person to ask win

options.label: Make them sort it out
options.detail: They do, badly.
options.storyHeadline: Made them sort it out themselves

options.label: Both go, you cover
options.detail: A terrible week for you, and a good one for morale.

headline: Someone's work has fallen off a cliff
body: It has been six weeks. They used to be your best.

options.label: Ask what's going on
options.detail: Something is wrong at home. They recover.
options.storyHeadline: Asked what was going on, and helped

options.label: Formal performance process
options.detail: They leave. Later you find out why.

options.label: Wait it out
options.detail: It either resolves, or it spreads.

gamble.loseText: It spread to the rest of the team.

headline: Everyone wants Fridays off
body: Four-day week, same pay.

options.label: Try it for six months
options.detail: Either it works, or reversing it costs you goodwill.

gamble.winText: Output held, and hiring got noticeably easier.
gamble.loseText: Output dropped, and reversing it cost you goodwill.

options.label: Four days at 90% pay
options.detail: Most people accept it, and it works.
options.storyHeadline: Moved to four days at 90% pay

options.label: No
options.detail: Straightforward, and not popular.
options.storyHeadline: Said no to the four-day week

headline: The company dog situation
body: Someone brought a dog. It has been four months. Nobody knows whose it is. It has a nickname and a bed.

options.label: Make it official
options.detail: One allergy complaint you handle badly. Worth it.

options.label: Find the owner
options.detail: The dog leaves. Nobody forgives you.

options.label: Do nothing
options.detail: The correct answer, and everybody knows it.

headline: Somebody wants a title, not a raise
body: "Head of" something. It costs you nothing and it costs you everything.

options.label: Give it
options.detail: Free, and three others ask within a month.

options.label: Give the raise instead
options.detail: More expensive, but there's no precedent to manage.
options.storyHeadline: Gave a raise instead of a title

options.label: Neither
options.detail: They leave within eight months.

headline: Your best engineer wants to become a manager
body: They would be a mediocre manager and they are an excellent engineer.

options.label: Let them try
options.detail: You lose an engineer and gain a mediocre manager.

options.label: Say no honestly and pay them more
options.detail: Resentful for a quarter, grateful for a decade.
options.storyHeadline: Said no honestly and paid them more

options.label: Invent a senior technical track
options.detail: A month of thinking. It solves this permanently.

headline: Somebody is leaving for a competitor
body: They gave four weeks and they're being decent about it.

options.label: Let them work the notice
options.detail: Awkward, dignified, correct.

options.label: Walk them out today
options.detail: Everyone else quietly updates their CV.

options.label: Counter-offer
options.detail: A real chance they take the raise and leave anyway.

gamble.loseText: They took the raise and left within the year anyway.

headline: The Christmas party
body: Small budget, or generous one.

options.label: Spend properly
options.detail: Two stories that last a decade.

options.label: Something modest
options.detail: Fine, and forgettable.

options.label: Cash bonus instead, no party
options.detail: Nobody remembers it, but everyone banks it.
options.storyHeadline: Gave a cash bonus instead of a party

headline: Someone brought their parent to a meeting
body: It's a salary negotiation. The parent has notes.

options.label: Handle it graciously
options.detail: Strange, memorable, and they stay for years.

options.label: End it and reschedule
options.detail: Correct, and slightly cold.

headline: Two of your staff are together and nobody has said anything
body: Everyone knows. One of them manages the other.

options.label: Move the reporting line
options.detail: Handled, with mild embarrassment. Correct.

options.label: Say nothing
options.detail: It ends badly, eighteen months from now.

headline: The thing keeps breaking on Fridays
body: Nobody knows why. It is always Friday.

options.label: Stop everything until it's found
options.detail: A week gone. It was something stupid.
options.storyHeadline: Stopped everything to find the Friday bug

options.label: Restart it every Friday morning
options.detail: Works, embarrassing, permanent.

headline: A supplier has gone quiet
body: Three unanswered emails and a full order book.

options.label: Find a second supplier immediately
options.detail: Costs something now. Safe forever after.

options.label: Keep calling
options.detail: Either they were on holiday, or they've gone under.

gamble.winText: They were on holiday. Everything resumed.
gamble.loseText: They'd gone under. You scrambled for weeks.

headline: Somebody suggests rewriting everything in a new language
body: They are half right, which is the problem.

options.label: Let them rewrite one piece
options.detail: Six weeks, and it proves the point sensibly.

options.label: Full rewrite
options.detail: Eight months of shipping nothing.

options.label: No
options.detail: They leave within a year.

headline: The demo broke in front of the customer
body: Badly, and they saw the error message.

options.label: Be honest and reschedule
options.detail: Some customers respect it. Some don't.
options.storyHeadline: Was honest and rescheduled the demo

gamble.loseText: They went quiet and never came back.

options.label: Talk over it and continue
options.detail: It works today, and costs you later.
options.storyHeadline: Talked over the broken demo and kept going

headline: You have too many products and none of them are good
body: Every one of them is halfway there.

options.label: Kill two of three
options.detail: Revenue drops now. It's worth far more in two years.

options.label: Hire enough people to do all three properly
options.detail: It buys focus, at a real cost to runway.
options.storyHeadline: Hired to properly support all three products

options.label: Continue
options.detail: Nothing improves. Nothing ever does.
options.storyHeadline: Kept all three products limping along

headline: A tiny customer is using 60% of your support time
body: They pay $90 a month.

options.label: Fire them as a customer
options.detail: A trivial revenue loss, and enormous relief.

options.label: Charge them properly
options.detail: They leave anyway, just a little slower.
options.storyHeadline: Tried charging the tiny customer properly

options.label: Keep absorbing it
options.detail: The support team notices. Morale takes the hit.
options.storyHeadline: Kept absorbing the tiny customer's support load

headline: Everything is on one person's laptop
body: Including things nobody else understands.

options.label: Spend a month documenting it
options.detail: Dull, essential, and it costs a little morale.

options.label: Carry on
options.detail: A real, if small, chance of a genuine crisis.

gamble.loseText: They left, and everything they knew left with them.

headline: An unexpected tax refund
body: $40,000 you had not counted on.

options.label: Straight into the bank
options.detail: Simple, and it buys real runway.

options.label: Bonus to the team
options.detail: Gone in a week, and it means something.
options.storyHeadline: Gave the tax refund out as bonuses

options.label: Spend it on marketing
options.detail: A real, if temporary, spike in signups.
options.storyHeadline: Spent the tax refund on marketing

headline: The accountant found something
body: You have been paying for a service you cancelled two years ago.

options.label: Claim it back
options.detail: Four months of phone calls, and it's real money.
options.storyHeadline: Clawed back two years of wasted payments

options.label: Just cancel it properly
options.detail: Simpler, and it still helps.

headline: Your prices have not changed in four years
body: Everything else has.

options.label: Raise them 20% for everyone
options.detail: A meaningful jump in revenue, and some loud complaints.

options.label: New customers only
options.detail: Slower, and nobody complains.
options.storyHeadline: Raised prices for new customers only

options.label: Leave it
options.detail: Margin quietly erodes, forever.
options.storyHeadline: Left prices exactly where they were

headline: A cheaper insurance quote
body: Half the price, from a company you have never heard of.

options.label: Switch
options.detail: Real savings, with a small chance it bites you later.

gamble.winText: It was fine. You saved the difference.
gamble.loseText: They refused a claim when it mattered.

options.label: Stay
options.detail: Expensive, boring, safe.

headline: The company car question
body: Someone has done the tax maths and presented it enthusiastically.

options.label: Yes
options.detail: A permanent, low-level argument about who gets which.

options.label: No
options.detail: Correctly, and without incident.

headline: You are owed money by someone who is nearly bust
body: Take a haircut now or wait and hope.

options.label: Settle for 40% today
options.detail: Modest, and done.

options.label: Wait
options.detail: Everything, eventually — or nothing, ever.

gamble.loseText: They went under. You got nothing.

headline: Currency moved against you
body: Nine percent, overnight, for reasons unrelated to you.

options.label: Hedge from now on
options.detail: No more surprises, at a small permanent cost.

options.label: Ride it
options.detail: It moves back, or it doesn't.

gamble.winText: It moved back. No lasting harm.

headline: A journalist wants to write about your industry
body: You'd be one of four companies mentioned.

options.label: Talk to them
options.detail: You might be the lead example, or barely a footnote.

gamble.loseText: You were the also-ran, barely mentioned.

options.label: Decline
options.detail: {RIVAL} is quoted at length instead.
options.storyHeadline: Declined to talk to the journalist

headline: Your website has been down for a day and nobody told you
body: A customer mentioned it in passing.

options.label: Build proper monitoring
options.detail: It never happens again.

options.label: Apologise and move on
options.detail: It happens again in eleven months.

headline: Someone made a video taking your product apart
body: Fairly, and it has 200,000 views.

options.label: Respond publicly and fix the issues
options.detail: They make a follow-up, and it's a good one.
options.storyHeadline: Responded publicly and fixed the issues

options.label: Say nothing
options.detail: It stays the top search result for two years.

options.label: Contact them privately
options.detail: They either quietly update it, or post the email.

gamble.loseText: They posted the email. It got worse.

headline: An award you could enter
body: Entry costs $3,000 and everybody knows it's mostly bought.

options.label: Enter
options.detail: It either goes on everything for a decade, or it's $3,000 gone.

gamble.winText: You won. It goes on everything for a decade.

options.label: Don't
options.detail: {RIVAL} wins it and mentions it constantly.

headline: A conference wants you to speak
body: Unpaid, four hundred people, two days including travel.

options.label: Go
options.detail: Two customers and a hire, for two days of your time.

options.label: Send someone else
options.detail: They come back energised. Half the value, none of your time.

options.label: Decline
options.detail: Nothing happens, either way.

headline: A pigeon has moved into the office
body: It has been three weeks. It is not leaving.

options.label: Call someone professional
options.detail: Done, and mildly sad about it.
options.storyHeadline: Called in a professional for the pigeon

options.label: Adopt it
options.detail: It appears in the company photo now.

options.label: Leave the window open and hope
options.detail: It invites another one.
options.storyHeadline: Left the window open and hoped

headline: Somebody registered your company name as a band
body: They are quite good. They have 40,000 monthly listeners.

options.label: Legal letter
options.detail: You look ridiculous, and they gain 20,000 listeners.
options.storyHeadline: Sent the band a legal letter

options.label: Sponsor them
options.detail: Unexpectedly excellent marketing.
options.storyHeadline: Sponsored the band using your name

options.label: Nothing
options.detail: People confuse you forever, occasionally in your favour.
options.storyHeadline: Ignored the band using your name

headline: The office plant has become important
body: It has a name, a schedule, and a dedicated group chat.

options.label: Buy nine more
options.detail: One dies eventually, and it is genuinely upsetting.

options.label: Say nothing and let it continue
options.detail: Correct, and it costs nothing.
options.storyHeadline: Let the office plant situation continue

headline: An intern automated their own job in three weeks
body: They now have nothing to do and have told you.

options.label: Hire them properly
options.detail: An excellent hire, and it shows immediately.

options.label: Give them something harder
options.detail: They solve that too.

options.label: Let the internship end
options.detail: They go to {RIVAL} and do it there instead.

headline: Your product was used in a crime
body: Creatively, and it was in the news.

options.label: Say nothing
options.detail: Signups jump. You feel strange about it.

options.label: Add a safeguard
options.detail: Three weeks of work, and it's the correct call.
options.storyHeadline: Added a safeguard after the incident

options.label: Make a statement
options.detail: It extends the story by another week.
options.storyHeadline: Made a public statement about the crime

headline: Somebody keeps stealing the good chair
body: It has escalated. There is a spreadsheet.

options.label: Buy twelve good chairs
options.detail: The golden age begins.

options.label: Assign the chair permanently
options.detail: Civil war.

options.label: Remove the chair
options.detail: Unity, through loss.

headline: The company is now a pub quiz answer
body: Someone sent a photograph. The question was unflattering.

options.label: Post it yourself
options.detail: Everyone loves you for a week.

options.label: Nothing
options.detail: It was already funny without you.
options.storyHeadline: Said nothing about the pub quiz

headline: A conference has put your name on a sign, misspelled
body: On the main stage, in three-metre letters.

options.label: Correct them
options.detail: Fixed by the afternoon. Nobody noticed.

options.label: Photograph it and post it
options.detail: Thirty thousand people notice, all of them warmly.
options.storyHeadline: Posted a photo of the misspelled sign

headline: Your office is on a street with a very silly name
body: It is on all your paperwork, permanently.

options.label: Lean into it
options.detail: It becomes part of the brand, genuinely memorable.
options.storyHeadline: Leaned into the silly street name

options.label: Use a PO box
options.detail: Dull, professional, forgettable.

headline: Somebody has been feeding a fox behind the building
body: There are now four foxes. It is a situation.

options.label: Stop it firmly
options.detail: The correct call, and not a popular one.

options.label: Do nothing
options.detail: The foxes end up in a national newspaper article about your company.

headline: A very large company has sent you a cease-and-desist for a joke on your website
body: The joke is good. Their letter is nine pages.

options.label: Remove it
options.detail: Free, and slightly humiliating.

options.label: Publish the letter
options.detail: Free press for a week, and an enemy for a decade.

options.label: Make the joke better and put it back
options.detail: They either escalate, or they give up.
options.storyHeadline: Made the joke better and republished it

gamble.winText: They gave up. You won this one.
gamble.loseText: They escalated. It got expensive and loud.

headline: Your co-founder has entered a competitive sport
body: Seriously. They train at 5am and talk about it constantly.

options.label: Sponsor them
options.detail: Brilliant internal morale, and mild absurdity.

options.label: Say nothing
options.detail: They're noticeably happier, and working slightly less.

headline: Team offsite, or bonuses?
body: Both cost something. Only one costs cash.

options.label: Team offsite
options.detail: A shared experience, off-site, on the company.

options.label: Bonuses instead
options.detail: Cash, kept simple.
options.storyHeadline: Gave bonuses instead of an offsite

headline: Rebrand the colours?
body: Nobody asked for this. Somebody wants to do it anyway.

options.label: Do it
options.detail: Nobody outside notices. Everyone inside feels new.

options.label: Leave it
options.detail: Nothing changes, correctly.

headline: Do you go to the industry dinner?
body: Free food, forced conversation, maybe something useful.

options.label: Go
options.detail: One useful conversation, or one wasted evening.

gamble.winText: One conversation turned into something real.

options.label: Skip it
options.detail: An evening back.

headline: Buy the domain you don't need?
body: You don't need it. You might, someday.

options.label: Buy it
options.detail: Tidy, and cheap enough not to matter.

options.label: Don't
options.detail: One less thing to renew.

headline: Update the website photos?
body: The old ones are three years and one rebrand out of date.

options.label: Update them
options.detail: A small, real bump in conversion.

options.label: Leave them
options.detail: Nobody's complained yet.
options.storyHeadline: Left the website photos as they were

headline: Someone wants to start a company book club
body: Three people will attend twice. It's still worth it.

options.label: Support it
options.detail: Small, cheap, genuinely appreciated.

options.label: Let it fade
options.detail: It fades on its own, no harm done.
options.storyHeadline: Let the book club idea fade

headline: Should the newsletter go weekly?
body: More frequent, more work, unclear if anyone reads it either way.

options.label: Go weekly
options.detail: Someone's whole Thursday, forever, in exchange for real signups.

options.label: Keep it as is
options.detail: Less reach, less effort.
options.storyHeadline: Kept the newsletter as it was

headline: Free lunch on Fridays?
body: Not expensive individually. Very expensive at scale.

options.label: Yes
options.detail: Everyone stays till three. Worth it.

options.label: No
options.detail: Nothing changes.

headline: Sponsor the local school's football kit?
body: A small, local, mostly invisible act of goodwill.

options.label: Sponsor it
options.detail: Nothing measurable. Everybody feels good.
options.storyHeadline: Sponsored the local school's football kit

options.label: Don't
options.detail: Nobody notices either way.

headline: Print business cards again?
body: Nobody has asked for one in two years. Somebody still wants them.

options.label: Print them
options.detail: Faintly retro, occasionally useful.

options.label: Skip it
options.detail: Nobody misses them.
